messages.subject: Re: data for covarying analysis
messages.body_plain:
Yong, here is a less elegant, but (I think) more transparent solution
for learning-about-R purposes:

words.1<-as.character(data.old[,1])
words.2<-as.character(data.old[,2])
strings.1<-paste(words.1, words.2)
strings.2<-rep(strings.1, data.old[,3])
strings.3<-strsplit(strings.2, " ")
strings.4<-sapply(strings.3, "[")
strings.5<-t(strings.4)
data.new <http://data.new><-as.data.frame(strings.5)

These steps could be nested into one line of code, but at the cost of
the transparency:

data.new <http://data.new><-
as.data.frame(t(sapply(strsplit(rep(paste(as.character(data.old[,1]),
as.character(data.old[,2])), data.old[,3]), " "), "[")))

Best. Earl Brown

messages.subject: collinearity in log regression / order in glm/lrm statement
messages.subject_clean: collinearity in log regression / order in glm/lrm statement
messages.body_plain:
hi all,

I have got a question concerning collinearity problems in log
regression models that contain only factors.

I would like to fit a log reg model with 10 factors. Many of these
factors are correlated  and sometimes several factors line up to
predict another variable.

following crawley 2007:327 I would like to proceed via stepwise model
simplification. so I start by fitting a maximal model that fits all
factors of interest, then inspect the parameters and remove the least
significant terms one at a time until only sig terms are retained.

I understand that in such a case a lot depends on the order the terms
are entered into the glm/lrm statement.
Every order threatens to produce a different result making it very
hard to simplify & arrive at the best model.

Just to make this a little more tangible one order yields:

	Estimate	Standard Error	Z	P
(Intercept)	-2.10182	0.76269	-2.756	0.005855	**
extern.role=other	-2.07738	0.41077	-5.057	4.25E-07	***
extern.role=subj	1.16069	0.54921	2.113	0.03457	*
intern.role=other	0.48494	0.43871	1.105	0.268999
intern.role=subject	0.64886	0.45148	1.437	0.15066
ani.head=inanimate	1.59185	0.47149	3.376	0.000735	***
def.head=indifinite	0.50145	0.32964	1.521	0.128205
ms.head=pronominal	1.0589	0.70766	1.496	0.134567
voice=passive	-0.02147	0.30234	-0.071	0.943385
embedding=right	-0.12032	0.53764	-0.224	0.822911
ani.SRC=inanimate	-0.13357	0.41725	-0.32	0.748887
def.SRC=indefinite	0.19649	0.34424	0.571	0.568143
ms.SRC=pronominal	0.43019	0.46176	0.932	0.351532

...and another one give me this:

	Estimate	Standard Error	Z	P
(Intercept)	-0.99467	0.67006	-1.484	0.1377
embedding=right	-0.21402	0.52266	-0.409	0.6822
ani.SRC=inanimate	1.00824	0.2408	4.187	2.83E-05	***
ms.SRC=pronominal	0.89323	0.42748	2.089	0.0367	*
intern.role=other	0.21496	0.42685	0.504	0.6145
intern.role=subject	-0.05195	0.39497	-0.132	0.8953
ms.head=pronominal	0.48387	0.65753	0.736	0.4618
def.head=indefinite	0.52654	0.33065	1.592	0.1113
def.SRC=indefinite	0.22336	0.34852	0.641	0.5216
extern.role=other	-2.11025	0.40909	-5.158	2.49E-07	***
extern.role=subject	1.01293	0.5304	1.91	0.0562	.
voice=passive	-0.03682	0.29988	-0.123	0.9023

I guess I could in principle try all orders
--> simplify every max model (until the minimal adequate model has
been arrived at)
--> and compare all minimal models via AIC (or something)

but that seem rather dull...can anyone maybe advise me on the best
practice for such a case?

thanks, guys and
cheers,
daniel

messages.subject: Problem with lookback
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I need help with very basic stuff regarding string manipulation.

I have strings like:

"*PAU: [4] cê sabe aqui como é que [/3] como é que tem que fazer esse
muro aqui / né //"
"*ROG: [12] aqui já tá dando [/4] aqui já tá dando a altura //"
"*ROG: [24] mas <olha [/1] olha> [/1] olha por cima pro sior ver //"

What I need is to insert the tag <r> in every instance of [/n], where
n is a number.

So I used gsub with this regular expression:

"/(\\d)\\]", "/\1\\]<r>"

Problem is, lookback does not retrieve the number between square
brackets. The output is this:

"*PAU: [4] cê sabe aqui como é que [/ #]<r> como é que tem que fazer
esse muro aqui / né //"
"*ROG: [12] aqui já tá dando [/#  ]<r> aqui já tá dando a altura //"
"*ROG: [24] mas <olha [/# ]<r> olha> [/ #]<r> olha por cima pro sior
ver //"

Where # is an unidentifiable character.

Any suggestion?

Best regards,
M.

messages.subject: Re: Problem with lookback
messages.body_plain:
Maryuale, also if those numbers have more than one digit (i.e. "10" or
higher) then your search_term in gsub should have a plus sign: "/(\\d+)
\\]". Otherwise, it will only find 0-9, but not 10-99, nor 100-999,
etc. Best, Earl Brown
